d: Champion Olympic cyclist Victoria Pendleton visits Wood Green, in search of a dog who she can co-parent with her mum. And lovebirds Shai and Orin meet Polo the lurcher.

t: The Secret Life of the Zoo
d: The keepers think pregnant elephant Thi is three months overdue. Rampant giraffe Meru relentlessly chases the females in his herd. And young giant anteater Oso arrives at the zoo.
Comic crime drama from Walter Presents. A tense rural standoff ensues when a desperate farmer tries to stop his cows being slaughtered. In French/subs.
Brian, who's 74, is taken to King's by ambulance after falling down some stairs. His partner Margaret discusses their life together and the challenges of his severe dementia.
This episode meets older patients at King's hospital who've had to show resilience in their lives. And junior doctor Jim tries to get some Lego out of toddler Zara's nose.
Chris suffers multiple injuries after a quad bike accident near Penrith. Cyclist Vivienne is in a bad way after her bike leaves the road on a notorious Cumbrian pass.

Morris hosts at Rigsby's Guest House in Hertford. His attempt to entertain his guests at a local zoo isn't a hit with everyone and a breakfast hold-up doesn't go down well.
David and Erica put on some classic Blackpool fun for their guests at The Fairway, as they take on some local zombies in a horror walk.
Robin welcomes his rivals to the converted Dent Station in the Yorkshire Dales, where he's organised a butchery competition. A few home truths about the group are revealed.
The B&Bers meet for one last time to confront their critics and find out how much they've been paid. And some of Robin's petty marks over the week are thrown to the group for discussion.
Allie and Cliff have decided to leave the UK and find their new forever home on beautiful Crete. What Grecian gems can Ben Hillman find for their £240k.
Julie and Amanda want a holiday home where they can unwind and relax in Lot-et-Garonne. Will a riverside townhouse or characterful stone house with land aplenty have that je ne sais quoi.
When Aykan and Cathy first visited Spain, they instantly fell in love with the relaxed lifestyle and now want a place to call home in Dénia. Lee Juggurnauth shows them what £200k can buy.
Leah Charles-King helps builder James and childcare practitioner Laura to find a permanent home in the Valencian countryside for their £90k budget.
Checkout assistant Jamie-Lea hopes to impress her guests with plenty of flavoursome food, on a night featuring shocking impressions and a dessert with a twist.
Farmer Chris plans an Italian menu. But how will his guests feel when he tells them that he's serving one of his home-reared pigs for the main.
Retired publican Christine's menu seems to have come straight out of packets, jars and bottles. But she has a few surprises up her sleeve..
Hummus maker and local food lover James plans a Middle Eastern-inspired menu packed with local produce and a sparkly dress code.
The final host, 50-year-old retiree and 'lady of leisure' Shelley, serves up a menu of tried-and-tested favourites. But can her guests get a word in edgeways.
Mum and daughter Ann and Rebecca kick off the competition at Grange Farm Park in Lincolnshire. But tensions bubble when one pair of guests discover they're the only ones without a hot tub.
Marilyn and Neil's Edgecliff Boutique B&B in Kent boasts breathtaking views. But will a slow breakfast leave their chances of winning balancing on a knife edge.
The B&Bers visit Vera's Kitchen and B&B in Gloucestershire, where Warren's forced to host solo. Will a game of bar billiards help to win the week, or will breakfast lower egg-spectations.
Father and son Bis and Deep are the final hosts, at The Preston Hotel in Yeovil. Their USP is value for money, but some guests think the furniture is more cheap than cheerful..
On an emotional payment day, the B&Bers air their grievances on everything from slow breakfasts to dusty chandeliers. Who will come out on top and claim the crown.

Doctors worry that a mechanic could lose his crushed arm. Dr Luke's decision not to cycle in the city is affirmed when treating a cyclist who's been hit by a car.
Dr Andrew Trezise is worried that a dirt biker has life-altering injuries after a crash. Dr Jonathan Papson fears for a showjumper who's been thrown off a horse.

George Clarke looks back at some amazing houseboats, including a wartime seaplane made into a bachelor pad, a writer's retreat in the shape of an egg and a Danish home floating on bottles.
In and around the beautiful villages of Haute Vienne in southern France, Sara Damergi helps recently engaged Michelle and Steve find the perfect family holiday home for their £100k budget.
Richard loves the seaside town of Sitges in northern Spain, and wants his very own holiday home there. Can Jasmine Harman find him the perfect place for his £210k.
Eileen from Birmingham wants the perfect holiday home on Spain's Mar Menor to take time out from her demanding job. Leah Charles-King shows her what £43,500 can buy.
Shelley loves the Greek islands so much that she's visited almost 30 of them. Can Laura Hamilton find Shelley and Adrian's dream holiday home on Zante, for £75,000.
Paula and Phil scour the pretty coastal resort of La Duquesa to find a holiday home for their £200k. Can a duplex built into the hills or a house that feels like home steal their hearts.
Yvonne and Graham want a bolthole in the charming seaside town of Alvor on Portugal's Algarve. Can Ben Hillman find their perfect place, close to the harbour and the beach, for £135k.
Planning enforcement officer Becky hosts an evening of modern home-cooking, including crispy croutons and a lamb shank stew. Two of her guests take a shine to one another.
Shoba serves an Indian menu, but her guests aren't impressed with her frozen fish curry. Can some Bollywood-style belly dancing save the day.
Drum tutor Rob hopes that his Thai-tastic menu will wow his guests - especially the object of his affections, Petrina.
Singing teacher Petrina hopes that her experience entertaining on cruise ships will give her evening the edge. And her salted caramel chocolate dessert serves up a surprise.
On the final night, Giovanni flies the flag for Sicily with some family recipes. But he has a tagliatelle tragedy.
Jill hopes to charm her rivals with her authentic 17th-century B&B, The Castle Arms Inn, in Snape, North Yorkshire. But will a bad night's sleep for two guests scupper her chances.
The B&Bers head off to the great outdoors at Eden Valley Glamping site in Armathwaite, Cumbria, where hosts Liz and Dave hope to convert their guests with their back-to-basics approach.
Neil and Mary welcome their rivals to Fernie Castle in Fife. There's plenty of traditional Scots splendour on show, but two guests aren't impressed by the continental breakfast.
The last visit of the week is to the Cadillac Kustomz Hotel on the Isle of Bute, where owners Brody and Rima hope to rock their guests' worlds with a music-filled retro retreat.
On payment day, there are curtain complaints and breakfast blues as the B&Bers iron out their issues, before they find out how much they've been paid and who's won the week.

In Hartlepool, the heli-medics treat a man who's been hit by a train. Cyclist Trevor suffers serious injuries after a collision. And in Cumbria, a biker needs emergency surgery.

Ken welcomes his rivals to The Wheatsheaf in Exning, near Newmarket. Ken claims to be the host with the most, but his sense of humour doesn't go down well with guest Nigel.
Sherrill hosts at the Sherwood Guesthouse in New Brighton on the Wirral, where some of her guests are stunned by the value for money, but Nigel goes looking for cleaning misdemeanours.
Mark and Rachael host at the ski-themed Big Bear Lodge in Shropshire, where an afternoon of canoeing raises a few laughs, but accusations of cheating cause a rift.

Glamorous 22-year-old Shanice plans an evening of sumptuous but risky food and scintillating conversation, about everything from lookalikes to riding polar bears.
Ex-estate agent Vivi serves a Norwegian feast inspired by her homeland, on a night that features ghost stories and nursery rhymes. But there's tension between two guests.
On the third night, Charlotte takes a risk with an Asian-inspired menu. But the biggest surprise comes when the group discover her ballerina past.
With a simple menu, children's entertainment manager David's sense of fun is the focus of his night and Neil finds himself sandwiched between Shanice and Charlotte..
Super-competitive sales director Neil, who resembles James Bond star Daniel Craig, hopes to raise the bar with a caviar starter and artistically angled panna cotta.
The competition kicks off at My Way Guest House in County Durham. Hosts Kaye and Lily pride themselves on cleanliness, so it's a shock when two guests make some dusty discoveries.
David and Sophie hope that their award-winning brekkie at The Old Orleton Inn in Shropshire will win them the week. But the portion sizes lead to some stomach-rumbling grumbles.
Amanda and Trudy host at the pet-friendly Ambles House in Northampton. The homely hospitality makes everyone feel like part of the family, but there's an uninvited guest at breakfast.
Richard and Harriet pride themselves on their high-end rooms at The Royal George in Tintern, Monmouthshire. Their guests lap up the luxury but some less-than-perfect scores shock the hosts.
It's the final day and the B&Bers meet one last time to settle some scores. After bathroom blues and cleanliness concerns are aired, the payments are revealed and the winner is announced.
Frank's all fired up over a rare 1946 Harley-Davidson Knucklehead at a hidden California compound. But will the devoted owner part with his pride and joy.

t: The Secret Life of the Zoo
d: There's a new arrival in the chimp group at Chester, elderly chameleon Mr Parsons has a romantic date, and Gaston the banteng bull has made three females in his herd pregnant.
A 32-year-old man and his 57-year-old dad have been shot dead in their Cambridgeshire homes. What turned a family child-custody dispute into a double execution.
Two men are dead after a child-custody dispute turned very nasty. The police have a prime suspect. But did the killer act alone or as part of a wider conspiracy.
A young man is treated for a severe reaction to a recreational drug, while 65-year-old Christine from Camberwell is brought in to King's by her friends after banging her head.
